Learn how to play "Blackbird" by The Beatles on the acoustic guitar!

In this lesson, we'll learn Blackbird by The Beatles on the guitar. A lot is happening in this tune - a fantastic song to practice different guitar techniques!

💡 Blackbird. This lovely The Beatles acoustic song, originally played by Paul McCartney, was released in the summer of 1968. It's part of the classic The White Album.

This tutorial will walk you through the details of the riffs and the three main beats. Check out JustinGuitarTabs to get verified tabs, chords, and lyrics to learn faster.

Playing Blackbird by The Beatles

There are several time signature changes in Blackbird! You'll play 3/4 at some parts, but the whole song mainly alternates between 4/4 and 2/4 time signature.

😅 Story Time! I had the pleasure of meeting Paul McCartney several years ago. I asked him about his fingerpicking style for this song. I misunderstood that the thumb bounces over between the root of the chord and the G string. After some research, I realized I was playing it wrong. In fact, to follow McCartney's technique, use your thumb and your first finger, so you kind of end up doing a bit of strumming with your fingerpicking. Much simpler to do, right? :)

I recommend you learn Blackbird one riff at a time. The first riff of this song has essential techniques, so it's the one you want to focus on learning. You'll need all the techniques in riff 1 to play the rest of the song. To get that proper McCartney sound, play those down and up strums with the first finger. Then, you'll also need to hit the G string with the down strum correctly. Make sure you nail that before learning the rest of this song!

🏅 Blackbird by the Beatles really is a bonafide acoustic guitar classic. It's like a rite of passage for all guitar players. Most people have a go at it at some point in their guitar journey! I'm hoping that this lesson will set you off on the right path.

Enjoy playing - it's great fun and even better for a party! :)

Learn to play "Heart of Gold" by Neil Young on the Guitar

In this lesson, we'll learn how to play Heart of Gold by Neil Young on the guitar. This classic song is a great choice for both novice and experienced players, offering a variety of levels to challenge your skills. Whether you want to keep it simple or strive for a note-for-note recreation of the original, this lesson has you covered.

Heart of Gold has three main sections: the introduction, the verses, and the chorus. The introduction features a small riff, followed by a chord sequence that forms the basis for the verses and the chorus. The song exhibits a certain dynamism, allowing you to either keep it simple or add complexity to make it sound closer to the original record.

Introduction

The introduction starts with the E minor seven chord, then briefly switches to the D chord, and then transitions back to the regular E minor. This sequence is then embellished with a little hammer-on technique that adds a touch of flair to the progression. The rhythm for this part emphasizes down picks, creating a steady and straightforward beat that sets the tone for the song.

Verses

The verses follow a similar progression, switching between the E minor, C, and D chords and the occasional G. It's important to note that the rhythm in the verses is not set in stone. Neil Young himself frequently changes his strumming pattern, making the song feel more organic and human.

Chorus

The chorus maintains the rhythm of the verses while incorporating a bit of variation. It follows a progression from E minor to G, then to C. As with the verses, you can add extra strums to enrich the rhythm and give it your personal touch.

Making the Song Your Own

One of the beauties of Heart of Gold is its flexibility. The chord progression and strumming patterns are not rigid and allow for a certain degree of personal interpretation. Listen to the original recording and play along with it to get a feel for the song's "time feel" - the human element that makes it groove. You can also check out various live versions of the song to see how Neil Young varies his performance and perhaps adopt some of his variations to make your rendition unique.

Wrapping Up

Learning to play Heart of Gold on the guitar is a rewarding experience. The song's structure and progression provide a solid foundation, while its flexible rhythm allows for personal expression. So grab your guitar, tune up, watch the video, and get ready to add this classic song to your repertoire. And remember, practice makes permanent!

How to play "All I Want Is You" by U2 on guitar

In this lesson, we'll learn how to play All I Want Is You by U2 on the guitar. This classic hit is a beautiful ballad that showcases U2's signature sound. It starts simple but builds in complexity, making it a great song to grow with as you develop your skills.

The song features a mix of basic chords and some more advanced techniques, but don't worry—we'll break it all down step by step. Whether you're a beginner or a more advanced player, there's something here for everyone. So, grab your guitar, and let's dive in!

Basic Chord Progression

At its core, All I Want Is You revolves around a simple chord progression. We primarily work with A and D chords, with an F♯ minor thrown in for good measure. Don't let that F♯ minor scare you off, though! We've got some great simplification tricks up our sleeve for beginners.

The song's basic structure is one bar of A and one bar of D. Occasionally, we swap out the A chord for the F♯ minor. This creates a lovely, rolling sound that's characteristic of the song.

Palm Muting and Adding Accents

One of the coolest things about this song is the palm muting technique. It's what gives the song its distinctive sound. If you're new to palm muting, don't worry! It's a technique where you lightly rest the side of your picking hand on the strings near the guitar's bridge. This creates a muted, percussive sound that adds texture to your playing.

In All I Want Is You, we use palm muting with a pattern of eight down strums per bar. It might feel a bit awkward at first, but with practice, you'll get the hang of it. And trust me, it's worth the effort—it really makes the song come alive!

Once you've got the basic palm muting down, we can start adding accents. These accents give the song its groove. We're putting emphasis on beat one, the "and" after beat two, and beat four. It might sound complicated, but it's all about feel. When you get it right, you'll know—it just clicks!

The Riff

The riff in All I Want Is You is where things get really interesting. It combines an acoustic guitar part with an electric guitar melody on top. Don't worry if you can't manage both parts at once—we've got a simplified version that captures the essence of the riff using just an acoustic guitar.

The simplified version uses A and D chords with some sus2 chords thrown in. A sus2 chord is just a regular chord where we lift off one finger, creating a slightly different sound. There's also an Easy Open Suspended Chords lesson that you can check out. It's these little details that make the song so captivating.

Advanced Strumming Pattern

We have an advanced strumming pattern that uses 16th notes for those of you looking for a challenge. I know that sounds like a mathematical nightmare, but it's really just about getting a feel for the rhythm. We'll break it down in the video so you can gradually build up to the full pattern.

Final Thoughts

Learning to play All I Want Is You is a journey. It's a song that can grow with you as you develop your skills. Whether you're just starting out with the basic chords or you're ready to tackle the advanced strumming patterns, there's always something new to discover in this U2 classic.

One of the best things about a song like All I Want Is You is that it's a great opportunity to develop your ear. I encourage you to listen to the original track and try to pick out the different elements we've discussed. Can you hear the palm muting? The accents? The sus2 chords in the riff?

Remember, the most important thing is to enjoy the process. Don't get discouraged if you can't nail everything right away. Every great guitarist started as a beginner, and with practice and patience, you'll be amazed at what you can achieve.

I hope this lesson inspires you to pick up your guitar and start playing. Watch the video for a detailed, step-by-step guide on how to play All I Want Is You. We'll look at each technique we've discussed and see some tips on how to practice effectively.

Keep strumming, keep practicing, and most importantly, keep having fun! Before you know it, you'll be playing All I Want Is You like a pro. Rock on!

Welcome to my Guitar Gift Guide 2025!

This list is perfect if you’re looking to buy something awesome for the special guitarist in your life… or if you’re a guitarist treating yourself. No judgement here!

I’ve got 10 great suggestions, ranging from approximately $35 to $700—though prices can vary significantly this time of year due to the numerous sales, so it definitely pays to shop around.

👕 Dig the Xmas Jumper Justin is wearing in this video? Grab it here!

These are not in any particular order, and please note that any of these companies hasn’t paid me to promote their products. Throughout the year, I received various products for testing, with no obligation to feature them. I’m just sharing what I genuinely like and use.

1. BlueChip Picks (~$35 to $75 each)

Let’s start with a shocker. I must have lost thousands of picks in my life… but I have a few picks I’ve kept for years because I look after them very carefully—they cost $75 each. Yes, you heard that right. Seventy-five dollars… for a single pick. And no, they’re not made of gold.

Sounds crazy, but honestly:

They feel incredible

They glide over the strings beautifully

They produce a fantastic tone

If you want to get a guitarist something special—something they probably wouldn’t buy for themselves—these are a great shout. They come in lots of shapes and thicknesses, so check what your favourite guitarist normally plays.

2. D’Addario Pick Holder 360 (~ $20)

I love this thing—much more useful than I expected when it first arrived.

If you’ve watched my livestreams, you’ll have seen the little table I keep beside me with all my picks and capos… and you might’ve even seen me knock the whole thing over once. Chaos! This little pick holder solves that.

The top tray keeps your frequently used picks ready to grab

There’s a storage compartment underneath

The bottom also acts as a protective lid, making it easy to throw it in your gig bag.

It even spins—an unnecessary, yet oddly satisfying feature. They’re $20 and should be available at most guitar retailers.

3. Boss Katana Go ($100 / £100)

The Boss Katana series remains the best bang-for-buck amp line available, and this little mini headphone amp, the Katana Go, is brilliant for its size. I take it on holidays so I can practice without annoying the family!

10 amp types

Loads of effects

Full editing via Bluetooth and a mobile device

And most importantly: it sounds mega

Usually around $100, depending on where you order it from!

4. D’Addario Backline Gear Transport Backpack (~$150–$250)

I love bags and luggage, so when D’Addario said they’d send their new Backline Gear Transport Pack, I was all in, and honestly, it’s fantastic. It’s designed for gigging musicians, but even if you play at home, it’s perfect for staying organised.

Highlights:

Front cable bay with clever dividers

Top compartment ideal for pedals, mics, and accessories

The laptop section in the back

Tons of pockets—super practical and very sturdy

It retails around $150–$250, depending on where you shop.

5. String Swing Guitar Hangers & Slat Wall System

People always ask about the guitar hangers behind me in my videos. They’re made by String Swing, an American company that continues to manufacture in the USA with excellent quality.

I use their slat wall panels with multi-arm hangers—easy to install, look great, and crucially… keep my guitars off the floor where my toddler can’t reach them. They offer a wide range of options, tailored to your specific space.

6. ToneWood Amp 2 (~$300)

If you missed the video Mike Dawes and I did on this, do check it out.

This little box is amazing for acoustic players. It attaches to the back of your guitar using magnets, and the effects come out of the guitar itself—no amp required.

Reverb, delay, modulation… all coming straight out of the wood. It’s wild! They’re around $300 and make a brilliant gift for any acoustic lover.

7. Bosch Powered Screwdriver (~$50) + D’Addario Peg Winder (~$10)

Many companies have attempted to release powered string-changing gadgets, but if you look backstage at a pro tour, most techs use a good power screwdriver with a tuning-peg bit.

After trying a few, the Bosch one is my favourite.

Super fast string changes

Adjustable torque

Forward and reverse

Does exactly one job—and does it properly

The screwdriver is around $50 / £50, and the peg-winder bit from D’Addario is about $10.

8. Boss RC-1 Looper (~$100)

One of the most fun toys you can buy for a guitarist.

The RC-1 is simple, reliable, and great for beginners:

No screens

No menus

No weird extras

Just press, play, overdub, stop. Brilliant for practice and songwriting. Most retailers sell it for about $100.

9. BeatBuddy Drum Pedal ($120 to $500)

Many people avoid metronomes because they think they’re boring, but those people often need them the most. Enter the BeatBuddy. It’s a drum pedal with numerous grooves that feel musical and enjoyable. You can even gig with it if you want drum backing.

Trigger fills, intros, endings.

Tons of styles

Sounds great

The Mini starts around $120, the standard model around $300, and the new upgraded version (which I haven’t tried yet) is around $500. Available through most online retailers or directly at singularsound.com.

10. Blues Immersion ($599 to $699)

I couldn’t finish this list without including one of my own creations. Blues Immersion is the course I’m most proud of building in recent years. It’s an intensive six-month program where we dive deep into:

The language of the Blues

Authentic licks and phrasing

5-pattern framework

Whole-neck confidence

History and artists of the genre

If you’re stuck in a pentatonic rut and ready to invest in yourself, check it out!

🎄 Final Thoughts

I hope this gave you some fun ideas, whether you’re shopping for a guitarist you love or treating yourself to something new.

Wishing you a fantastic festive season filled with love, laughter, and loads of music.

lessons.text:
Lights, Camera, Action: Studio Tour!

I'm excited to take you on a tour of my filming and recording studio and give you a behind-the-scenes look at how I create my YouTube videos! I will share detailed information about my gear, my settings, and how I organize everything for easy filming.

I still write, film, and edit all my videos by myself, so keeping everything simple and streamlined is my way to go.

The Importance of Set Arrangement and Distance

When it comes to filming, one of the most important things is your set arrangement. I see many people setting up too close to the wall, but having a bit of distance between yourself and the backdrop can make a huge difference. It can help you avoid casting shadows and create a better depth of field. I like to have a bit of space between myself and the background so the camera can focus on me while still having some interesting elements in the background.

Another thing to consider is your lighting. It's important to have a well-lit set to create a professional-looking video. A good lighting setup can make a big difference in the overall quality of your video. I use a main light, a fill light, and a backlight to create a well-lit set. Check out the tutorial for more details!

Filming Alone: Quick and Easy Setup

As a solo YouTuber, I need to have a setup that's quick and easy to use. Everything needs to be within reach and ready to go when I'm filming. I always have a guitar stand close by and a computer monitor to keep track of my sketches and outlines.

For filming, I use two Atomos drives to record my videos. These drives allow me to capture high-quality footage with ease. I also have a Quad Cortex for my electric guitar sounds and a Kemper for my acoustic guitar. A quick and easy setup is crucial because it allows me to focus on creating content rather than setting up equipment.

Preparing for Videos: The Importance of Preparation

When it comes to making videos, preparation is key. I spend a lot of time thinking about what will be in my videos and preparing the song or lesson. I like to create bullet points that outline the structure of the lesson and the topics I'll cover. They help me stay on track and ensure I cover everything I want in the video.

I also like to have a clear idea of what I want to say before I start filming. While some YouTubers prefer to have a script and storyboard, I like to do it off the cuff. Having a general idea of what I want to say allows me to be more natural and authentic in my videos.

The Importance of Cameras: Choosing the Right Cameras and Lenses

Choosing the right cameras and lenses is crucial for creating high-quality video footage. I use two Sony A7S3 cameras, which are great for creating high-quality video footage. Before these, I was using the Panasonic G5s, which are also great, but I had many problems with the autofocus function on those.

I use the GM Master lenses on my cameras. The main one I use is a 16 to 35-millimeter, which I set at around 30 millimeters. The little one I use for close-ups is a 24 to 70. I film in ProRes now, which has a massive file size, so I can't even save the files on the cameras. I save them on these little things called an Atomos drive. I've got two, one for each camera. The Atomos drives are really good because they put a big red circle around it when it's recording, so I know it's recording, and it won't stop without me knowing.

The Importance of Audio: Setting Up Your Audio Rig

Audio is just as important as your video quality because if your audio is bad, viewers won't stick around to watch your videos. I use a Head Rush on the floor for the audio from the Quad Cortex, and I have a microphone in my hat.

🎤 The hat microphone is essential because the volume doesn't change when I move my head around. When I used to wear a lapel mic, if I was looking at my strumming hand, it would get really loud, and then I'd look at the other hand, and it'd get quieter. I always had to muck around with balancing that!

I also have a microphone in the input that plugs into Logic. I usually have my audio set up on a different channel so that I can edit it separately from the video. This allows me to fine-tune the audio and remove any unwanted background noise.

Editing: Bringing It All Together

Once I've finished filming, it's time to start editing. I use FinalCut Pro to edit my videos, but there are plenty of other great editing software options. Editing can be time-consuming, but it's essential for creating a polished final product. I usually export the video in 16-bit 48 in PCM, which ensures that the video is of high quality and sounds great.

High-Quality YouTube Lessons

Creating high-quality YouTube videos requires a lot of time and effort, but it's ultimately worth it. A well-lit set, a quick and easy filming setup, and high-quality cameras and audio equipment can make a big difference in the overall quality of your videos.

👉 Have questions about this video? Tag me in the Community and ask me! :)

lessons.text:
Hey, how you doing? Justin here for a different lesson - not guitar related!

This video is way out of my comfort zone, but I wanted to share a few things with you! I'm feeling great mentally and physically - better than I've ever felt, and a lot of it is down to lifestyle changes I made for 2022. Sharing them with you might also positively impact your well-being, so why not give it a try! :)

😅 It feels a little weird not to have the guitar in my hands. I had to put one next to me! :)

Although I mention some brands in this video, please know that any of them sponsors this content. Now let's get stuck in!

10 Life-Changing Hacks You Should Try

Yep - life hacks this time; not guitar related! However, they will help you make the most out of your day and, ultimately, improve your guitar practice and playing. :)

#1 - AG1 (Athletic Greens)

You might have heard about AG1, or Athletic Greens, before, as there are loads of influencers constantly flogging this multivitamin. I first came across it in the Huberman Lab Podcast, and I trust what Andrew Huberman got to say, so I decided to give it a go.

I started drinking AG1 four months ago to kick off my day and immediately felt the results. This multivitamin has made a significant improvement in my overall vitality and digestive health! I switched from other multivitamins, and the change was noticeable.

🚨 I'm not a health influencer, and I don't have a discount code or kickback from AG1 in any way. I just rate it! I was taking multivitamins and pre/probiotics before - but this one feels different.

I recommend you check out AG1. It is expensive for what it is, but it really works for me. I'd taken other multivitamins before, but Athletic Greens made a huge positive impact on my health. Although I usually make healthy choices regarding my eating, I wasn't getting all the nutrients I needed because I definitely feel better taking this!

#2 - Cold Showers

Almost every day in 2022, I had a 2-minute cold shower at the end of my regular shower. I'm sure it's positively impacted my mental strength and resilience and helped reduce general anxiety. Now I feel weird if I don't start my day with that cold shock!

Plenty of science shows the benefits of cold showers, and it's not as horrid as it sounds once you've done it a bit! Start with just 10 seconds and build up over time. :)

I got into cold showers via the Wim Hoff Method, but it can be simpler than that - just slam on the cold water at the end of the shower!

#3 - Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu

I started learning Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in February 2022, and I absolutely love it. It's great for functional fitness, and I feel fitter overall than when I did more lifting at the gym. Sure, I have constant minor injuries, but it's been beneficial in almost every aspect of my life.

👍 I'd encourage you to go try it at a nearby club! Even if you think you're too old, unfit, busy, or whatever other excuses we use, BJJ can still be great for you - give it a try! ;)

Most places have a free trial; if you don't like it, then at least you tried something new! And if you're anywhere nearby, I train at Jay Butler BJJ in Yateley (Hampshire); it's an awesome club!

#4 - Meditation

These last few months, I've struggled to make time for meditation as much as I used, but I still get at least 3 x 15-minute sessions each week. I used to do it for 30 minutes daily!

I like the Waking Up app, but no matter which app you choose or if you just do it on your own, adding some mindfulness meditation to your life will improve it. Being more present and less distracted improves everything, including your relationships with others.

#5 - No Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR)

I discovered this recently, but No Sleep Deep Rest is incredible! It's a 10-minute session that feels like an hour's nap. For me, it's the perfect end to my lunch break to fire me up for the afternoon.

I'm up early and pretty active, so I often took a nap after lunch, but swapping it for NSDR has been brilliant. It's based on yoga principles of breathing in ways that are really relaxing! There are backing tracks for it all over the Internet - the one by Andrew Huberman is great!

#6 - Toilet Poetry

This is a pretty funny hack! It may not be life-changing, but it's a step in a positive direction. Many people, including me, take their phones into the toilet with them… I suspect we spend longer in there than needed because of it, and more often than not, we'll be on social media. Am I right?

A fun trick is leaving a book of poetry in the bathroom, so you can read it instead of staring at your phone! It's much better for the soul than social media. :)

#7 - Stoicism

I am a fairly committed stoic. I believe that the ideals to which the Stoic philosophy aspires are perfect for the modern age and solve many prevalent mental health issues.

You don't need to pay anyone or buy anything; there's nothing to worship and no rules to follow… It simply offers ways to change your perspective on life's challenges that make everything seem ok.

The concept that helps the most is ensuring we stop worrying about things beyond our control. Reflecting on the shortness of life helps me make the most of every day.

📖 Here are three of my favorite Stoic books: Donald Robertson, How to Think Like a Roman Emperor. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations. William Irvine, A Guide to The Good Life.

Many videos will introduce you to the important concepts quickly, and Ryan Holiday's content, like the Daily Stoic email, is also great! Experiment and see if the shift in mindset doesn't make you a happier human.

#8 - Think!

What do you really want out of your life? Many people seem to go through life without giving it much thought. You'll have a much better chance of getting your life somewhere awesome if you head in the right direction! Too often, people drift along, waiting for divine inspiration that never comes. I believe we make our own luck, so a little time now and then to think about where you are and where you want to be can pay huge dividends!

December is a great time to start this - most people feel the new year is a chance to renew and refresh, so plan it in advance! I recommend putting as many things into action right away - a running start to the new you!

#9 - Dog Walking, Pilates, and Yoga

Mobility, balance, and core strength are crucial for a healthy life. I do one Pilates class each week, and it feels great.

💡There seems to be a false perception that Pilates is for seniors and women. However, pilates was invented by a man, Joseph Pilates. :)

When done with the right instructor, pilates is physically very hard. Yoga is the same - I've done it on and off for years, and these days, I just tend to do a short series to wake my body up each day.

There is also increasing evidence of the benefits of Zone 2 Cardio, which means easy intensity, like going out for a walk with a dog! If you don't have a dog, you can borrow one from someone struggling to make time to walk their own dog! And if you don't like dogs (are you crazy?), try to get out for a walk for at least 30 minutes daily. :)

#10 - Music Therapy

Last but not least, let's remember all the many benefits of playing music. Studies in neuroscience show that learning music can enhance brain function, help you de-stress, and increase your empathy and emotional connections with yourself and others.

Playing music will also help your time management, as it requires consistent practice, developing that skill in other areas of your life, like exercise! It can help your listening skills and your math skills if you get into understanding music theory!

You'll develop patience and perseverance. It will help you learn to focus, maintain concentration and coordination… You'll get a sense of achievement as you progress, develop your confidence, and you might even make new friends!

I'm obviously biased - but I think learning to play an instrument is the best thing you can do for yourself after exercising and eating healthily!

🎁 Know someone who might benefit from learning music? Buy them a ukulele or a guitar (second-hand?) and help them get started with JustinGuitar! :)

What will you try? Have other hacks to share?

I hope you'll try some of these things and that they will help you find much happiness in the coming years! If you'd like to share your thoughts and other life hacks that positively impact your life, join the discussion and let me know. How did you feel about this life-hacks video? Will you give any of it a try? :)

💙 I wish you all the very best and a life full of happiness and laughter!

lessons.title: LIVE: Discovering Grant Green - Jazz Guitar Transcribing
lessons.summary: I had a fun Monday morning transcribing Green Dolphin Street by Grant Green.
lessons.text:
Watch Me Transcribe Grant Green Live! :)

Following up on my Jazz guitar lesson with Jens Larsen, I thought I should livestream my 1-hour Jazz guitar practice with you. :)

I've heard about Grant Green many times but never deeply explored his music before. So I decided to dig deeper into him and picked Green Dolphin Street to transcribe.

💡 Transcribing is a great way to develop your ear and learn new techniques and ideas that you can incorporate into your own playing. It takes patience, focus, and dedication, but it's incredibly rewarding when you finally nail a tricky passage or solo.

Green Dolphin Street is a popular Jazz standard that Green recorded in 1961. It's relatively easy; however, I used to know it in the key of C, but I'm transcribing it in E Flat today. Let's see how that goes!

💬 I plan to do some more Live sessions soon. Leave your suggestions here if you have any! :)

Then you'll want to graduate to a valve amp - which have a much higher quality tone. Fender Blues Junior is a great choice. Q:London Workshops? Would be nice but everyone loves flying somewhere nice for an "away workshop". It's nice to fly somewhere and be removed from everyday life. I've tried to offer London workshops before. Something to work on this year maybe. Q:How long does it take to make a song? Differs for everyone. Songs can take any amount of time. It can be pretty immediate to gradual few years. In a band we write a record in two weeks, which is very intense. Tweaking can go forever...a year of working on the record. At some point you just have to make a decision. Dry signal recordings in which you plug into a DI box and out of the DI to your effects etc as a separate feed. Then you are able to use a reamp box and feed it through a different amp for differing effects. It's cool, but can offer too many options - you just need to commit to a sound to get the end result. Q: Do you like heavy metal? Depends on what you call heavy metal. I like Metalhead and grew up listening to 80s hair metal. Bands like Guns & Roses, Motley Crue. I like Metallica, but never got heavier than that. Q:What's a good amp to play in public? Fender Blues Jr again. Q:What ear training do you recommend? Try my transcribing tips on the website. The problem is discerning which chords are used and the order. A good starting exercise is knowing which chords are used in a song but not the order. Play the song and transcribe when and where the chords are used. Q: BB King licks? Loads on the site - love them! Q: Do you like Stevie Ray Vaughan? Love him. Q: What's a good amp to use with a strat? Fender Blues Jr! No, I don't have a deal with Fender, I just really like this amp and its a relatively good price for a great product. Q: Can you do Christian music? Sorry, I'm not Christian so it's not my cup of tea. Q: Do you like country? Not a lot of it, but I love Neil Young, Brad Paisley. Q: Who was your guitar idol when you were younger? Keith Richards, Mark Knopfler, Chuck Barry, then later on Joe Satriani, Eric Johnson, Steve Vai, Joe pass, Mike Stern, Scoffield. Shifts according to the music I'm into at the time. Q: Do you have advice for older guitar care? I am very careful to use lemon oil on vintage guitars (not on maple). Every time I change strings, I let the lemon oil sit on the fret board for 5 minutes, then rub well with a soft cloth. I like to let the telecaster get a bit "scungy" and don't clean it as often. I use Adario brand cleaner that's non abrasive. Try to use products that are recommended for that product or ask at a guitar shop. Q: Should you use your arm to pull back rather than your thumb when playing chords to avoid hand fatigue? A mixture is best really. It's not great overall technique but when playing a lot of bar chords using your arm can be useful and should be be practiced especially to get a sense of from where you can create pressure other than your thumb. Another great technique is using your thumb to wrap over the base note. That will definitely alleviate fatigue when playing bar chords. Q: Any tips on helping kids? I started at six on ukelele. It's a great instrument to start small children on. When their hands are bigger, age 8 or 9, put them on a full sized guitar. Usually, I find children hard to teach. I don't like to teach kids until they know what type of music they like. It motivates them to learn. I might do a kids course one day... Q: Can you do a lesson on your song, Broken? I wasn't planning to, and need to revise it. I'll tab it out and put it on the site. Q: Trying to improve alternate picking. Does it improve over time? I am also revising my own technique as time goes on. Check out the website "Cracking the Code" if you are keen to get technical with your picking. I was sceptical at first, but it's very analytical a to how great packers pick. He uses a technique called "downward pick slanting" which I am now using and re examining as well as incorporating into some of my stuff. I did have an offer from his site in one of my newsletters. Check out the section "Masters of Mechanics". Q: Tommy Emmanuel? Tommy Emmanuel or Jeff Beck - in my humble opinion the best guitar players ever. Q: Will you do Arabic songs? Probably not, sorry but I have a full plate already! Q: You mentioned Courtney Violet as a great new artist last week. Anyone else? New David Bowie record. Incredible! Black Star is one of the finest, darkest and most powerful pieces I've heard. Also, the Anchoress, who is an incredible singer and recorded upstairs from me. "Confessions of a Romance Novelist" is her album. Q : Would you recommend waiting until the new Blues Lead course over the older version? I think you'd enjoy the new one. It's now 4 levels. Blues lead one is Essential Blues now. I think it's pretty good. Should be starting up in a week to ten days time! Q: What did you discuss with McCartney when you met? We discussed how to play Blackbird correctly and also, how strange it is to play tv shows. I was just flabbergasted to be talking to him! It was only ten minutes. He's a lovely chap! I've never met Eric Clapton although I would have liked to. Q: Are there any tips for a smooth transition from a lick to a chord strum...ie as in "That'll be the Day"? Practice the transition as a one minute change. Speed and timing are the key issues. If you can play consistently at very slow timing, the task is then to play at the right tempo, gradually speeding up in tempo as you progress. Practice playing to the song as you approach the 75% mark of the actual song tempo. Q: Plans to do any Tommy Emmanuel lessons? I was planning on doing two, Angelina and Mombasa. Tommy has videos out on both of these, but when he explains stuff, I have to figure things out myself and I wonder how others would find it? He's offered to do a lesson here for us. I am hoping next time he's in the UK, I'll have him here for lesson and I will help to slow things down for everyone can figure it out. He makes the hardest things look so easy and it takes a lot of practice! Q: How do you synchronize you right and left hand, especially when sweep picking? I don't even sweep pick very well. I'm not a fast guitar player, but anything I do, I start slowly and build tempo up. All the incredible players I know say the trick is to play slowly and accurately and build the tempo up over time. Nudge the tempo up only as you become really comfortable with the speed you are at. "Wood shedding", or spending hours and hours at the same song, building accuracy and speed with a metronome or a backing track is the thing to do! Q: Fixing tonation? I have a series coming out with Charlie Chandler, my guitar guru, on guitar maintenance sometime in the future. Q: How do you stay motivated on days when you don't feel like playing? I have so much to do, I have other things I can do when I'm not in the mood to practice. However, in the past, I would just get on with it. Treat it like it's a job, especially if you plan to make a career out of it. I am so thankful for such a cool job and existence and it's important to remember that others have jobs they hate. If it's your hobby, think about what you're in the mood for. Pick something you really want to play and have fun with. Think of enjoyment as the ultimate goal. Find the thing you love and spend your time doing it! Q: Will you do a Glenn Frey song? Yes I plan to do a Glenn Frey song or some more Eagles. Maybe The Heat is On? Still debating on which tribute lesson to do. Q: Are you planning more lessons on time signatures? Probably but I have other lessons to plan first. Q: Do you ever break strings while jamming? Yes, I've broken them in front of thousands of people but then I had a guitar tech off stage. Sometimes, when younger I would intentionally take a string off to work around it as an exercise. It helps you explore the finger board in ways you haven't and helps manage panic if you break one in front of an audience. Q: Is it possible to become a professional solo player without singing? Yes, there are loads of non singing pros out there. I am planning my own solo set without singing as I don't like my own voice. Q : Anything in the future with Marty? He has plans to come back at some point with cool stuff one day. He's got things going on now but I look forward to having him back. Q: If you had to choose one guitar, one amp, one pedal, what would you choose? Fender telecaster, a Timeline delay pedal (I love delay effect) and the Lazy J 20 amp. I love the sound of the Tone King Imperial amp as well. It's next in my purchase list. Q: How can I feel a strumming pattern in a song? You don't feel it, you listen for it. Listen, try to find it from something you've heard/learned before , or try to copy it from an understanding of how rhythm works. I have an book on transcribing rhythm patterns that would be helpful. Q: Any views on travel guitars? I have a couple. I don't like the sound of ones with a small body. The one I use the most has no head stock (can't remember the name of it) Q: What hoodie am I wearing? It's Patagonia. Q: It would be amazing if you interviewed Guthrie. Yes, it would be. I should try to hook up with him. Q: Any thoughts on adding amp settings to the videos? For most of my videos, I use the profiling amp. It's a copy of another amp. So it would be hard to translate... Q: Do you wear a hat inside or just for the videos? I was just discussing this yesterday...it's like a disguise for me. Loads of people don't recognize me without the hat which is kind of handy and cool for me! No, I don't wear one all the time. Q: What happened to the keyboard that was on the floor? It was a controller keyboard. I upgraded to a big one, under all my stuff...I play a bit but not really talented. I enjoy it. Some stuff I do is a lot easier to explain on keyboard. Q: Wish You Were Here? Being redone at the moment, along with a stack of other stuff, like Life on Mars (beautiful chords), Lady Rider - tricky stuff in it...so many beautiful riffs. Also more Motörhead...been mostly getting the Blues course up and running. More playing next week on the live show after the buffering nightmares of today. Hopefully I'll have exciting news about the Blues course next week. Weekly Riff is set aside for now as we work on other things. Have a great week, time for pizza

Howdy guitar friend,

Hope this newsletter finds you well and that you're having a GREAT start to the year! :) If you're up for trying new stuff this year and missed my life hacks video, give it a try. Howdy Guitar Friend,

Hope this newsletter finds you safe and well and finding plenty of time to enjoy playing the guitar. As usual, it's been very busy around here, the renovation project is coming to a close, and I'm hoping to move into my new studio in July. Super exciting! But geez it's been eating my time, so many decisions to make and things to sort out. Mega thank you to our developers Mike and Ben (and designers Cass and Babs), who just released the redesign of our Songs pages! Now you'll easily find out which lessons are the newest, which are in the app, have tabs, etc. It's really user-friendly - I think it looks awesome, and I hope y'all dig it as well. The new lessons for Grade 4 are almost all done. Just a few Rhythm Maestro lessons to film! I just released the first lesson of the E Shape Major module - but they're all ready to go. Oh, I feel this first lesson is actually the most complete barre chords guide I could ever make! More on that below. I've also been working on a new Songwriting and Production course, some extracurricular content, and exciting projects that will be released this second semester. And believe it or not - I'm already planning content for next year. :) But first things way first... let's check out what's on this month's menu!

June Highlights The Ultimate Guide To Easy Barre Chords Song Lessons... and 1M subscribers! New Major Scale Maestro lessons JustinGuitar StarStudents Life Stuff...

📖 Read The Full Newsletter!

lessons.title: Join the Wish You Were Here at 50 Intro Challenge
lessons.summary: A community celebration of one of the greatest guitar songs ever written!
lessons.text:
There are guitar songs everyone knows… and then there’s Wish You Were Here.

Pink Floyd’s classic turns 50 this year, and to celebrate, I teamed up with Sony and the Pink Floyd team to create a super fun challenge for you! I released a brand new lesson for the iconic song—rebuilt from the ground up and split into five levels so every player can join in, no matter your experience.

Now I want the whole JustinGuitar community to get involved.

Learn the intro. Upload your take. Enter to win rare WYWH50 merch.

This isn’t a competition. It’s a sweepstake. That means it’s not about being the best player—it’s about celebrating the song together. All you have to do is:

Head to the Wish You Were Here lesson on justinguitar.com

Learn the intro at your level

Upload your take to YouTube

Add it to the Student Performances tab on the lesson page

And you’re in.

What you can win

Thanks to the Sony and Pink Floyd teams, we have some incredible, limited edition WYWH50 items to give away:

The ultra-rare Wish You Were Here 50 fire extinguisher (only 150 in the world!)

The official WYWH anniversary t-shirt

The Diver mug

The full 50th Anniversary box set packed with restored concert footage, unreleased mixes, clear vinyl artwork, and more!

If you love Pink Floyd, this is a once-in-a-lifetime piece of history to be part of.

Why this matters

Wish You Were Here is one of the most emotional, musical intros ever written. It’s where so many of us first fell in love with the acoustic guitar. This challenge is a way for all of us to:

Learn something meaningful

Share our playing

Celebrate a legendary piece of music

See the global JustinGuitar community come together!

Whether you’re a total beginner or a seasoned player, your version is welcome. Truly.

Deadline

All entries must be submitted by December 11. Don’t leave it to the last minute—pick your level and start playing today.

Ready to join in?

Let’s celebrate the music we love, let’s honour 50 years of an absolute classic, and let’s fill the Student Performances tab with beautiful versions from around the world!

🍀 Good luck!

lessons.title: How to Win 4 Private Classes with an Approved Teacher!
lessons.summary: Submit a video of your progress and get a chance to win private lessons with an Approved Teacher. Open to students worldwide!
lessons.text:
Share Your Progress. Win Private Lessons.

We're launching a new way to celebrate your journey—the Student Performances x Approved Teachers campaign! Whether you're strumming your first chords, working through a tricky riff, or showing off a full song, we want to see it. We'll choose one inspiring performance each month to win four private one-on-one lessons with a JustinGuitar Approved Teacher. It's our way of cheering you on and helping you take the next step. It's not about being perfect—showing up, sharing your progress, and being part of a supportive global community of learners.

🧐 Got Questions?

Here's everything you need to know before submitting your video! Scroll down to check out the FAQ. 👇

→ What kind of video should I submit?

Any video of you playing something you've learned from a JustinGuitar tutorial! It can be a full song, a riff, or a solo—as long as it's from a lesson we've published and listed in the Songs section on our website.

→ Where do I upload my video?

Go to justinguitar.com/student-performances and follow the simple steps to upload your video.

→ Who are the teachers giving the private lessons?

All lessons are taught by JustinGuitar Approved Teachers—experienced, friendly, and hand-picked by Justin. Teacher availability will rotate each month, so you won't be able to choose who you get, but you're in great hands either way!

→ How are winners chosen?

It's not about being perfect. We seek progress, passion, and the courage to share your playing. Justin and the team will pick one inspiring submission every month.

→ Can I enter more than once?

Yes! Feel free to submit new performances any time! The more you share, the better your chances.

→ Is this open to students worldwide?

Yes—wherever you are in the world, you can join in. Just note that lessons are conducted in English.

→ What do winners receive?

Each monthly winner gets four private one-on-one lessons (50 minutes each) with an Approved Teacher—one per week for a full month. As the campaign grows, more prizes may be added!

→ Does my video need to be public?

It needs to be public or unlisted on YouTube so we can view it and share it on the Student Performances page.

→ Will a teacher see my submission?

Yes! Our Approved Teachers will check submissions; you might even get some feedback or a shout-out on your performance.

🍀 Ready? It's your time to shine! Submit your performance here, and good luck. :)

lessons.title: World String Change Day Giveaway & New Video Series Launch
lessons.summary: Celebrate World String Change Day with us—refresh your tone, learn something new, and maybe even win the ultimate guitar care setup!
lessons.text:
At JustinGuitar, we believe changing your guitar strings shouldn't feel like a chore—it should feel like a fresh start.

That's why we're thrilled to team up with D'Addario to celebrate World String Change Day with something special: a huge giveaway and the launch of a brand-new video series all about string care and guitar maintenance.

Win the Ultimate Guitar Bundle

We're giving away an Ultimate Guitar Maintenance Bundle worth almost $600 to kick things off. This carefully curated prize pack includes:

12 sets of D'Addario strings (your choice of type and gauge)

String maintenance kit

String change mat

Pro-quality guitar cable

AutoLock strap

Rechargeable tuner

Capo

... and a few more surprises. Whether beginner or seasoned, this bundle has everything you need to keep your guitar sounding and playing its best.

💡 How to enter: It's simple—head over to our post on Instagram, Facebook, Community, or YouTube and leave a comment with your question about guitar strings or string maintenance. Entries close on June 9, and we'll announce the winner on June 10.

🆕 New Video Series: All About String Changes

To accompany the giveaway, we're launching a new video series focused on all the questions guitar players ask about strings—like how often to change them, how to choose the right set, and step-by-step tutorials for stringing different types of guitars. It's practical, beginner-friendly, and packed with useful tips. So even if you don't win the giveaway, you'll still walk away with a better-sounding instrument.

🥳 Celebrate World String Change Day with us—refresh your tone, learn something new, and maybe even win the ultimate guitar care setup!

lessons.title: Playin' It Forward: We're crossing new borders!
lessons.summary: We just sent guitars—and a whole lot of joy—to young athletes in Brazil. Thanks to you, Playin' It Forward is going global.
lessons.text:
Howdy, guitar friend,

Remember our Playin' It Forward program—our initiative that helps new players who cannot afford an instrument get started with a free guitar?

We've sent out over 150 guitars across the US and UK, and even fulfilled a few in Europe! We're wrapping up a 20-guitar batch in the US and preparing a new 50-guitar batch in the UK with our awesome friends at Andertons. How exciting is that! :)

None of this would be possible without incredible students like you, supporting JustinGuitar by purchasing our products, making direct donations, and spreading the word in online communities and on social media around the globe. 💙

But as you can imagine, expanding internationally has its challenges. Due to logistics limitations, we've had to keep most of our shipments within the US and the UK. That's why this next step means so much to us…

With the help of Tagima Guitars, who kindly provided instruments at cost, we're thrilled to kick off this new chapter by gifting guitars to 10 young athletes from a social project led by BJJ College from Black Belt Melqui Galvão.

Melqui takes discipline very seriously and ensures that the athletes receive their guitars, follow a practice routine, take care of their instruments, document their progress, and engage with their lessons.

🤼 As you might know, I train BJJ, so linking my two passions is awesome. Maybe I'll meet up and train with some of these kids one day - and hopefully they'll go easy on me! :)

The guitars are being distributed among athletes who live both inside the BJJ College social project houses and independently. They're also getting access to the JustinGuitar Lessons & Songs App! They're excited to share a bit of their progress online, so keep an eye out for our social media.

✨ Check out their Instagram: @isaquelimajj | @angelus_lutinhajj | @guilherme_souzajj | @zangado.bjj | @eve.azevedojj | @gabigordobjj | @marcos_jiu01 | @gabi_guedesbjj | @gabrielfonjj | @thiagaoteam

Thanks to Tagima, the largest Brazilian guitar and bass manufacturer globally in Latin America, the US, Canada, China, Japan, and more. 🌎 Their support made this Brazil expansion possible!

What's Next?

Connecting with these young athletes—eager, disciplined, and passionate about learning—has deepened our love for Playin' It Forward and our mission to make JustinGuitar and high-quality guitar education as accessible as possible.

Many have come from incredibly challenging circumstances, and their dedication to Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu represents a real shot at changing their lives. Seeing their enthusiasm for music as a way to express themselves and find balance is truly special.

Their story also inspires us to support other forms of learning and basic needs alongside music when appropriate. We've learned from connecting with the BJJ College athletes that some of them, despite their high performance on the mats, often lack access to quality English education (among other things), which is essential for traveling and succeeding as international competitors.

So we're currently exploring how we might sponsor a full year of English lessons for these young champs. We'll tell you more when the time comes. :) This is just the continuation of our mission to teach the world to play, every little bit of support makes a difference.

We've also decided to take things a step further and make it official that anyone who cannot afford a paid JustinGuitar product can request it for free. It's easy and simple to apply—just a little help to keep the music going. We also decided to keep many upcoming new site features completely free to registered students, plus we're committed to another year of excellent Live Classes and masterclasses offered for free in our Clubs. These changes will soon be announced and reflected on the Playing' It Forward, Donation, and Store pages.

How can you help?

If you're wondering how to support all this, keep doing what you're doing! Whenever you use the site, purchase a course or some merch, or tell a friend about JustinGuitar, you're helping us grow this mission.

And if you've got a moment, head over to our Instagram post to give Tagima a big thank you for making this possible—and to cheer on the amazing young athletes who are now learning guitar with us. Your words of encouragement mean the world. 🌍🎶

That's it for now. :)

Laters, Justin & Team

Win Big and Give Back with the JustinGuitar Big Raffle! 🎸

Have you ever dreamed of owning a stunning PRS Custom guitar? Or maybe you've wanted to take your guitar skills to the next level with exclusive lessons and premium courses? Well, now's your chance! The JustinGuitar Big Raffle has incredible prizes worth over $20,000. Best of all, every £5 entry goes toward a cause close to our hearts—helping aspiring musicians through the Playin' It Forward program.

👉 ENTER THE RAFFLE HERE!

What's the JustinGuitar Big Raffle All About?

At JustinGuitar, we believe in the power of music to transform lives. Playing an instrument can lift spirits, build confidence, and bring joy. That's why we've kept most of our content free, making quality guitar education accessible to everyone. But we know that for some, even getting a guitar to start with can be a challenge. That's where the Playin' It Forward program comes in.

This initiative provides free guitars to those who need them most, helping people from all walks of life embark on their musical journeys. We've sent out around 100 guitars, each a ticket to a brighter, more musical future.

The Prizes

The raffle is brimming with exciting rewards. Here's what's up for grabs:

Grand Prize: A gorgeous PRS Custom 24 from the limited Wood Library 10-Top collection, valued at over £5000. This is a dream guitar for any player, combining stunning looks with top-notch playability.

Blues Immersion Class 2 Spots: 10 lucky winners will secure a place in this sought-after course, valued at $699 each. Dive deep into the Blues and elevate your playing!

Private Lessons with Justin: Four winners will enjoy a one-on-one online session with me, worth $699 each. These personalized lessons are designed to help you grow as a musician and tackle challenges.

Lifetime Access to the Practical Music Theory Course: 14 winners will gain access to this premium course, valued at $299 each, forever. Master the theory behind the music and apply it directly to your playing.

How Does It Work?

For just £5 per entry, you can join the raffle and stand a chance to win any of these amazing prizes. But that's not all—your contribution will help fund the Playin' It Forward program, ensuring more people can experience the joy of learning guitar.

Why Your Support Matters

Every ticket you purchase helps us put guitars into the hands of those who need them. We've seen firsthand the difference a guitar can make in someone's life, offering a creative outlet, a sense of accomplishment, and a lot of fun. With your support, we can reach even more people, expanding the program and ensuring that financial barriers don't hinder anyone's musical dreams.

Join Us!

The JustinGuitar Big Raffle is your chance to win incredible prizes while making a real difference in the lives of others. So why wait? Click the link in the description to enter the raffle, grab your tickets, and be part of this amazing journey. Together, we can spread the joy of music far and wide.

💙 We're Playin' It Forward, one strum at a time! Thank you. :)

lessons.title: JustinGuitar is Playin' It Forward - Free guitars for those in need!
lessons.summary: Howdy guitar friend, nothing can stop you from learning to play. Apply here for a free guitar.
lessons.text:
Howdy guitar friend,

I hope you're in good spirits and with your favorite guitar within arm's reach. :)

I'm reaching out with immense excitement and a heart full of gratitude to share something brewing in my mind for quite some time – a project very dear to my heart, Playin' It Forward.

From the early days of JustinGuitar.com, my dream has always been to make learning music accessible to everyone.

I've witnessed the transformative power of music in people's lives, and learning an instrument can catalyze happiness.

That's why I've kept nearly all of JustinGuitar.com free, to ensure that quality music education is available to as many people as possible.

However, a realization struck a chord with me. Some folks who could benefit from the therapeutic joy of making music can't even afford a guitar to start with!

So that's where Playin' It Forward comes in.

💡 How It Works

Playin' It Forward is not just a project; it's a movement to break down barriers and make guitar education inclusive.

It's about reaching out to those who may be going through a tough time and providing them with the means to find comfort, expression, and joy through making music.

It's an initiative based on trust; not many questions are asked! All students need to do is to have a free account on the site and fill in a simple form.

💙 How Can You Help? Share The News!

I'm incredibly grateful for the support we've received over the years. Now, I'm inviting you to join me in making music accessible to all.

Whether you're a longtime member of our Community or just discovering JustinGuitar, your involvement can make a significant impact.

Please consider sharing Playin' It Forward with people who can benefit the most from this program.

Other ways of supporting us are by getting a 1:1 With Justin, donating, or contacting us if you have an electric guitar you no longer need. :)

I hope you enjoy this news, and I cannot wait to hear your feedback.

Rock on,

Justin Sandercoe
